job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: When buying packaged snacks, students often get confused by the information printed on the labels. First, look at the ingredient list, which is always arranged by weight. The ingredient listed first is present in the largest quantity, not the smallest. Many people assume that if sugar is not the first ingredient, the food is low in sugar, but manufacturers often use multiple names for sugar like syrup or dextrose to hide the total amount. Second, check the nutrition facts table carefully. The values provided are usually per serving, not for the entire packet. If you eat the whole bag, you are consuming multiple servings and thus more calories than the label suggests. Third, understand the symbols. A green dot indicates the product is vegetarian, but it does not mean the food is free from chemicals or additives. Finally, pay attention to dates. An expiry date indicates when a product is no longer safe to consume, whereas a 'best before' date refers to the peak quality of the food. Always store products as instructed, because the date is only valid if the packaging remains sealed and stored in a cool, dry place as recommended by the manufacturer.

items.evidence: The ingredient listed first is present in the largest quantity, not the smallest.
items.q: A biscuit label lists wheat flour first and salt last. What does this order tell you?
options: It has more flour than salt
It has more salt than flour
It has equal flour and salt
It had flour mixed in before salt
items.explain: Ingredients are listed by weight, so the first one, flour, is present in the largest amount.

wrong.why: thinks the first ingredient is the smallest amount
thinks the list order means nothing about amount
thinks the order shows the order of mixing

items.evidence: Many people assume that if sugar is not the first ingredient, the food is low in sugar, but manufacturers often use multiple names for sugar like syrup or dextrose to hide the total amount.
items.q: A cereal lists rice first, then glucose syrup, dextrose and sugar. What can you conclude about its sugar?
options: Its sugar may be high under several names
It is low in sugar, as rice is first
Its only sugar is the one named sugar
Its sugar is highest because sugar comes last
items.explain: Syrup and dextrose are other names for sugar, so the total sugar can be high.

wrong.why: thinks sugar not being first means little sugar
thinks only the word 'sugar' means sugar
thinks the last ingredient is the largest amount

items.evidence: If you eat the whole bag, you are consuming multiple servings and thus more calories than the label suggests.
items.q: A chips packet has 3 servings of 150 calories each. Riya eats the whole packet. How many calories?
items.explain: The label value is per serving; eating three servings gives three times 150, which is 450 calories.

wrong.why: thinks the whole packet equals one serving
divides by the servings instead of multiplying
adds the number of servings to the calories

items.evidence: A green dot indicates the product is vegetarian, but it does not mean the food is free from chemicals or additives.
items.q: Meena's snack packet has a green dot on it. What does the dot tell her?
options: It has no chemicals or additives
It is healthy to eat every day
It is still before its expiry date
items.explain: A green dot only shows the food is vegetarian; it may still contain chemicals or additives.

wrong.why: thinks a green dot means no additives
thinks any mark on a label means healthy food
mixes up the symbol with the date information
